machine: local Apple Silicon arm64 macOS; Zig 0.15.2; Python 3.14.6

statement.private_witness: Bitcoin mainnet genesis and block-one headers, 80 serialized bytes each
statement.description: Linked private headers, byte-exact SHA256d, target checks, ordered pair Poseidon2 root. Both profiles use the same normalized program, assignment, public root, and FRI schedule.

generic_sparse_wide_gate.command: python3 src/frontends/s31/s31.py build src/frontends/s31/examples/bitcoin_header_pair.s31.json --lowering sparse-wide-gate --out zig-out/s31/generic-pair; then three s31.py trial runs on that package and the same assignment

interpretation: The joined two-header profile is about 2.00 times slower excluding FRI proof of work (646 versus 323.327 ms) and its proof is about 2.33 times larger. Joined excluding-FRI-PoW still includes a small, unmeasured interaction grind, whereas generic excludes both grinds. The generic trial reports internal proving time from a package process; joined time is measured inside the Zig test, so setup and verifier times should not be directly compared. All three repetitions use the same witness and proof transcript. This is a negative local cost result, not evidence of throughput or recursive performance. Keep generic as the default; a purpose-built SHA round AIR is needed for a likely gain.
